questions.question: Gross profit of R820 000 on sales of R2 460 000 gives a gross margin of:
Gross profit on COST of sales equalling the intended 50 percent mark-up tells the partners:
options: The pricing policy was achieved — no large undetected markdowns, theft of stock before sale, or recording errors

questions.question: Net profit on sales for the year is:
An indicator only becomes meaningful when it is:
options: Compared — against last year, the budget, the policy or a similar business

subtopics.title: The Operating Cycle: Four New Indicators

questions.question: With cost of sales R1 640 000 and average stock R190 000, the stock turnover rate is:
options: 8,6 times a year — shelves refill about every six weeks

questions.question: The stock holding period and the stock turnover rate are:
options: The same fact in two dialects — refills per year against days per refill
Only comparable in a manufacturing business

questions.question: Average debtors of R54 000 against credit sales of R1 476 000 gives a collection period of:
Paying creditors at 24,3 days on 30-day terms means:
options: Nothing — the creditors' period has no interpretation
About six days of free credit are being handed back, unless an early-settlement discount justifies the speed

subtopics.title: Gearing and Return: Risk and Reward

questions.question: The debt-equity ratio of R138 000 to R765 800 is:
options: 0,2 to 1 — low gearing, little dependence on borrowed money

questions.question: A case for gearing UP exists when:
options: The bank offers a bigger loan
The business earns more on borrowed money than the borrowing costs — here, well above the loan's 12 percent

questions.question: Average equity for the return calculation is:
options: R734 300 — the average of opening R702 800 and closing R765 800

questions.question: The return on average partners' equity of 57,3 percent is judged against:
options: The risk-free alternative of roughly 8 to 10 percent in a fixed deposit — remembering the partners' labour also sits inside the return

subtopics.title: Liquidity and the Art of the Comment

questions.question: The current ratio and acid-test ratio are:
options: 4,1 to 1 and 2,1 to 1 — short-term debts covered even without selling stock

questions.question: A very high current ratio can itself be criticised because:
options: Idle cash earns almost nothing — over-liquidity wastes money that could expand the business or reduce the loan
It always means stock is unsellable

questions.question: The four parts of a full interpretation comment, in order, are:
options: Figure with its comparison, trend, cause, consequence or advice

questions.question: A rising current ratio is only good news if:
options: Paired indicators like the stock holding period confirm it is not just unsold stock piling up

questions.question: The stats-sheet picture says indicators are:
options: Small numbers that stand for a big performance, like goals per game

questions.question: A policy mark-up of 50 percent with an achieved margin of only 44 percent on cost signals:
options: Goods leaking — stolen before sale, quietly marked down, or misrecorded

questions.question: The coach's first rule for any stat is:
options: A stat means nothing alone — every number needs a next-to: last year, the plan, or a rival

questions.question: The rand's lap through the business runs:
options: Shelf to promise to cash — stock, then debtors, then bank

questions.question: Whether 42 days on the shelf is acceptable depends on:
options: The trade — fine for hammers and paint, terrible for bread

questions.question: Paying suppliers early with no discount is best described as:
options: Politeness at the shop's own expense — giving back free credit

questions.question: With money out for about 55 days and suppliers paid at day 24, the gap is financed by:
options: The shop's own money — which shortening the cycle would release

questions.question: The verdict on liquidity — safe, and slightly lazy — rests on:
options: Four times cover of short-term debts while over R130 000 dozes in the bank earning almost nothing

questions.question: Gearing as a volume knob means:
options: Low is safe, higher is louder — the right setting depends on how steady the earnings are
The knob only turns one way

questions.question: The return of 57,3 percent against roughly 9 percent risk-free supports the conclusion that:
options: The partners should close the business
The investment is sound even after mentally pricing the partners' labour
The bank deposit was the better choice

questions.question: The four-beat bar for exam comments is:
